title: Sustainability
intro: Fewer, better things — made to be worn for years, not seasons. Here's what that means in practice, and where we still have work to do.

sections.heading: Materials
sections.body: We build our collections around natural fibres — wool, cotton, linen, silk — sourced from mills we've worked with for years, chosen for durability first. We're moving toward certified organic cotton and responsibly sourced wool across the line, season by season, rather than relabeling the whole catalog at once.

sections.heading: Small Batches
sections.body: Every style is produced in limited runs against forecasted demand, not speculative volume. It costs more per unit. It also means far less overproduction and far fewer markdowns driving unsold stock to landfill.

sections.heading: Built to Last
sections.body: Construction choices — French seams, horn buttons, fully lined outerwear — are made so a garment survives years of wear and repair, not one season. A well-made coat is the most sustainable coat: the one you don't replace.

sections.heading: Where We're Still Working
sections.body: We don't yet have a formal take-back or resale program, and our packaging isn't fully plastic-free. Both are on our roadmap — we'd rather say so plainly than overstate where we are today.
